overall: Atlanta reached a running max of 89.6°F by 12:50 ET, but temperatures have since dropped sharply to 78.8°F — a decline of nearly 11°F — with a strongly negative velocity of -9.0°F/hr. This rapid cooling pattern, combined with no wind and an elevated dewpoint of 71.6°F, is consistent with convective activity such as a thunderstorm outflow or rain-cooled air mass moving through, suggesting the daily peak may already be in.
forecast_obs_notes: Three of four models (GFS 89.9, ECMWF 90.3, HRRR 89.9) cluster tightly just above the current running max of 89.6°F, while NBM at 87.5°F has already been surpassed. The even ensemble model signals 90–91°F at Tier 1 high confidence (58%), but the odd ensemble's 87–88°F call at only 12% (Tier 4 – Avoid) carries negligible weight.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely scenario is that 89.6°F is the final TMAX or extremely close to it — the sharp temperature collapse after the peak strongly argues against a meaningful afternoon recovery. The GFS/ECMWF/HRRR consensus of ~89.9–90.3°F aligns almost perfectly with the observed running max, giving moderate-to-high confidence that the day's high is effectively locked in near 89.6°F. A minor upward revision toward 90°F is possible if convective cooling is brief and temporary, but the -9°F/hr velocity makes a significant rebound unlikely.
